title: Rules Across Streams
subtitle: Act 2.0: one action loads the streams its decision needs, checks each at the version it loaded, and commits its events to all of them at once, or to none.

nodes.label: Enroll
preconditions: the course has a free seat
nodes.description: .on({ Enroll }, { maxRetries: 1 }).loads(Seats, (data) => `course-${data.course}`, ["SeatTaken"]). It loads the course's Seats before checking its rule, may emit SeatTaken to it, and commits Enrolled and SeatTaken together, guarded by both streams' versions.

nodes.label: Register
nodes.description: .on({ Register }).loads(Email, (data) => email(data.email), ["EmailTaken"]). One Email stream per address, keyed by an HMAC of it, loaded before the rule.

nodes.label: ChangeEmail
nodes.description: Loads Email twice: the old address (may emit EmailReleased) and the new one (may emit EmailTaken). Frees the old and takes the new in one commit.

nodes.label: Enrollment
nodes.description: One enrollment per student and course. Enroll and Waitlist check their rules here, with the loaded Seats in hand.

nodes.label: Seats
nodes.description: One stream per course. Its schema is its invariant, checked on every fold, so no action can overfill a course, whichever action emits SeatTaken.

nodes.label: User
nodes.description: One stream per user. Register and ChangeEmail check their rules here, with the loaded Email streams in hand.

nodes.label: Email
nodes.description: One stream per email address: an ordinary state the app declares, not a hidden framework stream. A stream name can't be forgotten, so the stream is keyed by an HMAC of the address, never the address itself.

nodes.label: SeatTaken
nodes.description: Owned by Seats. Enroll may emit it because its .loads lists it; it commits to course-<id>.

nodes.label: EmailTaken
nodes.description: Owned by Email. Commits to email-<address>.

nodes.label: EmailReleased
nodes.description: Owned by Email. Frees the old address when the user changes it.

nodes.label: Book
preconditions: the room is free at that time
nodes.schema:
room: string
from: time
to: time
nodes.description: .on({ Book }).loads(Room, (data) => `room-${data.room}`, ["RoomReserved"]). Loads the room's reservations before checking the slot.

nodes.label: Booking
nodes.description: One booking per guest request.

nodes.label: Room
nodes.description: One stream per room. Its schema refuses overlapping intervals on every fold.

nodes.label: RoomReserved
nodes.description: Owned by Room. Book may emit it because its .loads lists it.

nodes.label: Transfer
nodes.schema:
from: string
to: string
amount: number
nodes.description: .loads(Account, (d) => d.from, ["Debited"], "from") and .loads(Account, (d) => d.to, ["Credited"], "to"). The same state loaded twice, each load named.

nodes.label: Transfer
nodes.schema:
from: string
to: string
amount: number
nodes.description: One stream per transfer.

nodes.label: Account
nodes.description: One stream per account.

nodes.label: Transferred
nodes.schema:
from: string
to: string
amount: number

nodes.label: Debited
nodes.description: Owned by Account. Listed on the "from" load.

nodes.label: Credited
nodes.description: Owned by Account. Listed on the "to" load.

nodes.label: ReserveItem
nodes.description: .loads(Product, (data) => data.product, ["StockReserved"]). Loads the product's stock before checking it.

nodes.label: Order
nodes.description: One stream per order.

nodes.label: Product
nodes.description: One stream per product.

nodes.label: StockReserved
nodes.description: Owned by Product. ReserveItem may emit it because its .loads lists it.

nodes.label: Waitlist
nodes.description: .on({ Waitlist }).loads(Seats, (data) => `course-${data.course}`). No events listed, so it's a read: the rule sees Seats, but Seats isn't part of the commit, and isn't checked when it lands.

nodes.label: Logout
nodes.description: .on({ Logout }).loads(UserSessions, (data) => `sessions-${data.user}`, ["SessionEnded"]). Frees a slot on the user's count in the same commit that ends the session. Freeing is an action: app.close can't append to another stream.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.description: One stream per login.

nodes.label: UserSessions
nodes.description: One stream per user, counting active sessions. Its schema caps the count on every fold.

nodes.label: SessionEnded
nodes.description: Owned by UserSessions. Logout may emit it because its .loads lists it.

scenarios.title: One action, two streams
scenarios.summary: Ann enrolls in course c1. Enroll loads the course's Seats, checks its rule with both states, and commits Enrolled and SeatTaken in one step.

steps.say: The rule: a course holds at most **30** students. Each course's **Seats** live in a stream of their own; each enrollment lives in another. In plain event sourcing an action sees only its own stream, so **Enroll can't check the seats**.

In Act 2.0, Enroll adds one line: `.loads(Seats, course, ["SeatTaken"])`, and `{ maxRetries: 1 }` so a lost race is decided again. It loads the course's Seats for its decision, and may commit **SeatTaken** to it.
**Ann** enrolls in course **c1**. Enroll loads two streams: her own enrollment, new, and through `.loads`, the course's **Seats** at v11, with 12 of 30 taken.

The rule "the course has a free seat" passes with Seats in hand. Then the commit: **each stream is checked at the version it was loaded at**, and only then do **Enrolled** and **SeatTaken** land together.
...and **SeatTaken** to **course-c1**, in the same commit. Both streams were checked against the versions Enroll loaded, so nothing it decided on had moved.
Both events share one **correlation**, and each records what caused it: the event stream shows it. That's the audit trail of one decision across two streams.

scenarios.title: The last seat
scenarios.summary: Carla and Bob try for the last seat at the same moment. Both load the course at the same version. Carla's commit lands. Bob's version check fails, so nothing of his is written; his retry reloads Seats, and the rule refuses.

steps.say: **Carla** enrolls. Enroll loads her stream and **course-c1** at v28: 29 of 30 taken.
At the same moment, **Bob** enrolls. He loads course-c1 at the same **v28**. Each rule passes, on the same last seat.
Carla's commit lands first: both versions still match, so **Enrolled** and **SeatTaken** land together. The course moves to v29, **30 of 30**.
Bob's commit expected course-c1 at v28, and it's at v29. **The whole commit fails: nothing lands on either stream**, not even on Bob's own, which didn't move (`ConcurrencyError`).
Enroll's `maxRetries: 1` runs the action again with **fresh loads**: course-c1 at v29, 30 of 30.

steps.reject: the course has a free seat
steps.say: Now the rule sees the truth, and refuses Bob. A refusal he can act on, instead of an overfilled course.
Seats' schema says **taken ≤ capacity**, and it's checked on every fold. So no action can overfill a course, whichever action emits SeatTaken.

scenarios.title: A read isn't guarded
scenarios.summary: Dee joins the waitlist of a full course. Waitlist reads Seats for its rule, but lists no events on the load, so Seats stays outside the commit.

steps.say: **Dee** joins the waitlist. Waitlist loads her stream and reads **course-c1**: `.loads(Seats, course)`, with no events listed. That's the muted line: **a read**.
The commit covers only what it appends to: **her own stream**. Seats isn't checked, so if a seat frees up just now, Waitlisted still lands.
That's the trade: a read costs no conflicts, but guards nothing. A decision that must be refused when a stream moves appends to it.

scenarios.title: A unique email
scenarios.summary: Each email address is an ordinary Email state of its own. Registering loads it and takes it in the same commit as the user's own event.

steps.say: Uniqueness is just another state: one **Email** stream per address, recording who holds it. No unique index outside the store, no saga. A stream name can't be forgotten, so it's keyed by an **HMAC of the address** (`email-7f3a`), never the address.
**Ann** registers with **ann@x.io**. Register loads her own stream and the Email stream for that address: new, no holder.
The rule "the email is free" passes. One commit, both streams checked: **Registered** to user-42 and **EmailTaken** to **email-7f3a**.
...and **EmailTaken** to **email-7f3a**, in the same commit.

scenarios.title: Taken, then changed
scenarios.summary: Ben tries Ann's address and is refused. Then he changes to a free one: the old address is freed and the new one taken in one commit.

steps.say: **Ben** tries to change his email to **ann@x.io**. ChangeEmail loads Email twice, named `old` and `new`: his own address, and Ann's, held by user-42.
The rule refuses: the address already has a holder.
Ben picks **ben@z.io** instead. Both load again, and the new one is free.
One commit appends to three streams: **EmailChanged** to user-77, **EmailReleased** frees **ben@y.io**, and **EmailTaken** takes **ben@z.io**, each guarded by the version it was loaded at.
...**EmailReleased** frees **ben@y.io**...
...and **EmailTaken** takes **ben@z.io**. Three streams, one commit, each guarded by the version it was loaded at.
Had any of the three streams moved since it was loaded, **nothing** would have been written, and the action's `maxRetries` would retry with fresh loads.

scenarios.title: No double booking
scenarios.summary: Dana books room R1 from 10:00. Eli then asks for 10:30, which overlaps, and is refused.

steps.say: The rule: no two bookings of a room overlap. Each **Room** has a stream of its own; each booking another. **Book** loads the room it books.
**Dana** books room **R1** from 10:00 to 11:00. Book loads room-r1: 9:00–10:00 is taken.
The slot is free. One commit appends **Booked** to Dana's booking and **RoomReserved** to **room-r1**.
**Eli** asks for room R1 from **10:30** to 11:30. Book loads room-r1 again.
10:30 overlaps Dana's slot, so the rule refuses Eli. Room's schema would refuse an overlap too, whichever action tried.
steps.reject: the room is free at that time

scenarios.title: A transfer
scenarios.summary: Moving 50 from account A to account B appends to three streams in one commit. A second transfer of 100 is refused.

steps.say: The rule: a transfer debits one account and credits another, both or neither. **Transfer** loads **Account** twice, naming the loads `from` and `to`.
Move **50** from account **A** (80) to account **B** (20). Transfer loads its own stream and Account twice, named `from` and `to`.
"Enough funds" holds. One commit, three streams, each checked at its loaded version: **Transferred**, **Debited** to acct-a, **Credited** to acct-b. A debit without its credit can't happen.
Now move **100** from A, which holds 30.
The rule refuses it. Nothing is debited, nothing is credited.

scenarios.title: Only what's in stock
scenarios.summary: An order reserves 2 of the last 3 units. The next order for 2 is refused.

steps.say: The rule: reserve only what's in stock. Each **Product** has a stream of its own; **ReserveItem** loads it before deciding.
An order reserves **2** of product **p-7**, which has **3** in stock.
"Enough stock" holds. One commit appends **ItemReserved** to the order and **StockReserved** to **product-p7**.
Another order asks for **2**. Product p-7 loads with **1** left.
The rule refuses it, and Product's schema (stock ≥ 0) would too. Had the stock moved since the load, nothing would have been written either.

scenarios.title: Freed at logout
scenarios.summary: A user holds 3 of 3 sessions. Logging out ends the session and frees a slot in one commit, so a slot is never lost to a crash in between.

steps.say: **Ann** logs out. Logout loads her session and **sessions-42**: 3 of 3 slots in use.
One commit: **LoggedOut** ends the session, **SessionEnded** frees the slot. Both land or neither does, so there's no moment when a slot is lost.
Freeing is an **action**, on purpose. `app.close` retires a stream without running any action, so it can't append to another stream: free the slot first, then close.
